decisions.quote:
In this study, we built upon the work of Skerbetz and

Kostewicz (2013) by investigating the effects of across-

activity choices in isolation and Lane, Royer, et al. (2015)

by involving teachers in every stage of the research process.

We examined across-activity choices during classwide

reading instruction with three elementary students during a

40- to 44-min reading block.
decisions.location: Purpose, p. 79, lines 257-269 (Reference list, p. 92, lines 2131-2139)
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind target 0 identify Skerbetz and Kostewicz (2013) as the tested original study whose finding on the effects of across-activity instructional choices in isolation during reading instruction on student academic engagement is re-tested here (whereas Lane, Royer, et al., 2015 supplied the teacher-involvement research process and compared two choice types in writing).

decisions.quote:
Regarding TAE, all three students increased in level
and positive relative and absolute changes (range = +15

to +41). In addition, Maricela displayed significant

increases in AAE. Decreased variability was observed

during intervention for Fiona (TAE only), Maricela (all

variables), and Oscar (TAE only). These findings replicate

those by Skerbetz and Kostewicz (2013) who observed

similar increases without involving teachers in the research

process.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind code the outcome as successful. In the Discussion, the authors state an explicit overall verdict that their findings of increased academic engagement across the three students in the single-case withdrawal design replicate the findings of Skerbetz and Kostewicz (2013).

decisions.quote:
In this study, we replicated and extended previous

inquiry by investigating the effects of across-activity choices offered by third-grade teachers during reading instruction to

participating students with behavioral (one with internalizing and two with internalizing and externalizing patterns) and
academic needs.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind code the record type as replication. The study collected new direct observation data on three third-grade students in a single-case withdrawal design to re-test the finding of Skerbetz and Kostewicz (2013) that across-activity instructional choice increases student academic engagement during reading instruction.
